feature: Size mode reads the element you are pointing at
summary: Point at a button, a switch or a settings row in Measure's Size mode and the outline now wraps the whole thing and reads its real width and height. Before, a button read nothing at all, a switch read a 12 by 12 sliver of its knob, and a row stopped at its label text.
setup: Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next. Open queue/audits/2026-08-23-measure-00-capture.png, press i for Measure, and set the mode chip to Size.

try.do: Point at the blue Save Changes button, anywhere on it, including over the words. It should read 124 px by 30 px and never change as you move across it.
Point at the grey Reset button next to it. 72 px by 30 px.
Point at the dead centre of a green switch, right on the white knob. It should read 42 px by 24 px, the switch, not the knob.
Point at the empty space in a settings row, between the label and the switch. 624 px by 44 px.
Now point at the row's label text instead. Same 624 by 44.
Press ] twice from a row. The pick should grow to two rows, then to the whole card, always containing what it just showed.
Point at the grey page background outside the cards. Nothing should appear at all.
Click once on the button. Two calipers land, 124 and 30, in one undo step.

evaluate: When you sweep the pointer across a button, does the readout hold perfectly still, or does it twitch enough to make you doubt the number?
Pointing at the middle of a switch gives you the switch. Is that what you expected, or did you want the knob and now have to press [ to get it?
The row reads 624 wide, which is the row, not the 656-wide card it sits in. Is the row the thing you wanted measured?
Half the pane reads nothing at all (the whitespace inside cards, the gaps between them). Does the silence feel right, or does it feel broken?
Is one press of ] a big enough jump, or does the ladder skip past something you wanted?
rough: The empty text field reads 218 px wide when it is truly 220. A 1 px border between two whites puts the boundary reading on its inside flank at both ends. Pinned in tests so it cannot get worse, not fixed.
The card reads 652 wide when it is truly 656. Its outline is white on near-white under a drop shadow, so the edge is genuinely soft.

Point exactly ON a divider between two rows and the pick jumps to both rows at once, because a boundary under the pointer cannot be the element's own edge. Correct, but it looks like a glitch if you did not expect it.
The band of whitespace between two cards reads as a 652 by 20 element. It is honest (that band does have a top and a bottom) but it is not an element, and Gap mode is the right tool for it.

Nothing here was seen with human eyes this session: screen recording is blocked for this agent, so the play-test was run numerically through the shipping code over the real capture, plus stability sweeps across each element. The feel of the outline following the pointer is unverified.
